name: Phone state and numbers
plain: Lets the app see call state, the SIM and the phone's number.
meaning: Reveals carrier, SIM info and in some cases the user's number. Android restricts device IDs such as IMEI to privileged apps since Android 10.

android.store_policy: Play: identifiers policy bans persistent IDs from this API for ads
android.note: Android 10 (API 29) removed non-resettable identifiers (IMEI, serial) for non-privileged apps.

ios.note: iOS never exposes phone number or IMEI; CTCarrier returns placeholder values since iOS 16.4.

limits.headline: Can see call state, SIM and carrier info on Android; iPhone shows no number
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the Phone permission prompt
can: Tell whether a call is active
See your number on Android with the phone numbers permission
cannot: See the IMEI or serial number on Android 10 and later
See your number or IMEI on iPhone
Get real carrier names on iPhone 16.4 and later; it shows placeholders
limits.differs: Android gives call state and SIM details after a prompt; iPhone never exposes the number or IMEI.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app see whether you are on a call, plus details about the SIM and the phone's number.
story.for_you: A prompt asks for phone access. If you allow it, the app can tell whether you are on a call and may see your carrier or SIM. The app can pause itself when you get a call.
story.for_makers: Apps like music and games pause during calls. Others use the carrier info to pick a language or a network setting. Older apps abused it to grab device IDs, so it has been trimmed.

use_cases.example: A music app pauses when a call comes in and resumes after.
A game pauses a match when you get a call.
A video call app lowers quality when a cellular call starts.
A run tracker pauses when you take a call.
An analytics SDK reads the carrier to report network type.
A fraud tool reads SIM changes to spot a swapped SIM.
A call center app knows when the agent is on a call.

story.android_note: Android 10 removed non resettable IDs like IMEI and serial for apps without privilege.
story.ios_note: iPhone never exposes the number or IMEI. The carrier API has returned placeholder values since iOS 16.4.

technical_bounds: No IMEI for ordinary apps on either OS
Phone number still exposed on some Android versions with READ_PHONE_NUMBERS
Cannot read the number on iOS

linkedin.how: Phone Number is on the Apple label (Linked To You, optional on Play). Members enter it for two-step verification and CLEAR identity checks. Android phone state permission was seen in an older build.

history.change: CTCarrier deprecated; returns static placeholder values
IMEI, serial and other hardware IDs require privileged permission
Non-resettable device IDs blocked for normal apps
